stanzas: 關關雎鳩，在河之洲。
窈窕淑女，君子好逑。
參差荇菜，左右流之。
窈窕淑女，寤寐求之。
求之不得，寤寐思服。
悠哉悠哉，輾轉反側。
參差荇菜，左右采之。
窈窕淑女，琴瑟友之。
參差荇菜，左右芼之。
窈窕淑女，鐘鼓樂之。
orig.credit: Classic of Poetry (Shijing), Odes of Zhou and the South

stanzas: Guan, guan, cry the ospreys [?], on the islet in the River.
The modest and graceful good girl: a fine mate for the lord.
Uneven grow the floating-hearts; to left and right one seeks [?] them.
The modest and graceful good girl: waking and sleeping he seeks her.
He seeks her and does not win her; waking and sleeping he thinks of her.
Long, oh long! He tosses and turns from side to side.
Uneven grow the floating-hearts; to left and right one picks them.
The modest and graceful good girl: with zither and lute he befriends her.
Uneven grow the floating-hearts; to left and right one plucks [?] them.
The modest and graceful good girl: with bells and drums he delights her.
Guān guān jūjiū, zài hé zhī zhōu.
Yǎotiǎo shūnǚ, jūnzǐ hǎo qiú.
Cēncī xìngcài, zuǒ yòu liú zhī.
Yǎotiǎo shūnǚ, wù mèi qiú zhī.
Qiú zhī bù dé, wù mèi sī fú.
Yōu zāi yōu zāi, zhǎn zhuǎn fǎn cè.
Cēncī xìngcài, zuǒ yòu cǎi zhī.
Yǎotiǎo shūnǚ, qín sè yǒu zhī.
Cēncī xìngcài, zuǒ yòu mào zhī.
Yǎotiǎo shūnǚ, zhōng gǔ lè zhī.
rom.credit: Romanization: The Epoch Institute (Hanyu Pinyin (tone marks, modern readings))

notes: line 1.1: 'guan guan' imitates the birds' call. The bird 雎鳩 (jūjiū) is traditionally taken as an osprey or fish hawk; the identification is uncertain, hence [?]. 河 'the River' in early texts is the Yellow River.

line 1.2: 窈窕 (yǎotiǎo) is read as 'modest, retiring' or 'graceful, slender'; 君子 (jūnzǐ) 'lord, nobleman, gentleman'. 逑 'mate, match'; the variant 仇 means the same here. 好 read hǎo ('good'); some read hào ('loves').

line 2.1: 荇菜 (xìngcài) is a floating water plant, Nymphoides peltata (floating-heart). 流 literally 'flow, drift'; the Mao commentary glosses it as 'seek'; others read 'pick as they float'. Hence 'seeks [?]'.
line 2.3: 思服 'thinks of, keeps in mind' (服 glossed as 懷 'to cherish'). Variant 弗 for 不, same sense.
line 3.2: 琴瑟 (qín, sè) are two plucked zithers, the qin of 7 strings and the larger se; 'zither and lute' is a loose equivalent.
line 3.3: 芼 (mào) is glossed 'choose, pluck' or 'cook, prepare'; the variant 薅 means 'pull up'. Hence 'plucks [?]'.
line 3.4: 樂 read lè ('delight'); some read yuè ('make music for'). The subject 'he' is unstated in lines 2.2 to 3.4 (the gentleman of 1.2 is the usual reading).
rom: modern standard readings; old readings (e.g. 參差 cēncī, 芼 mào) as in dictionaries. No tone sandhi marked.
